extracted.intended_audience: Applicants and their agents (patent attorneys/agents) filing PCT international applications and practitioners handling international search and supplementary search procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory requirements governing the international search, written opinion, and supplementary international search procedures under the PCT (including sequence listing handling, limits on subject matter searched, unity/fees/protests, timing, contents, forms, languages, and communications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of documentation to be consulted by the International Searching Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Searching Authority must consult the 'minimum documentation' and, where it has more than the minimum documentation at its disposal, is obliged to consult that additional documentation to the extent permitted by its facilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists of national collections and periodicals are enumerated (e.g., selected Offices, PCT publications, ~135 technical periodicals). The obligation extends beyond minimum documentation where available and practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of later-submitted missing parts or corrected elements on international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search will usually be carried out on the basis of the application containing the missing parts or the correct elements or parts. In the case of incorporation by reference of correct elements or parts, the erroneously filed elements or parts remain in the international application but will not have to be considered for the purpose of international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refs: Rule 20.5, Rule 20.5bis. If missing parts are incorporated later by reference they are ignored for search purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation and additional fee if missing parts notified after search begun
rubrics_metrics.description: If inclusion or incorporation by reference of missing parts or correct elements is notified to the International Searching Authority only after it has begun to draw up the international search report, the Authority may invite the applicant to pay an additional fee for that purpose, payable within one month to the Authority; if not paid, the Authority will draw up the search report and written opinion without taking into account the missing parts or corrected elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invitation specifies amount and one-month time limit; applicant pays additional fee directly to ISA; failure to pay results in parts being ignored in search.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirement when disclosure of nucleotide/amino acid sequences present
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the ISA finds that an international application contains disclosure of one or more nucleotide and/or amino acid sequences required to be included in a sequence listing pursuant to Annex C and a compliant sequence listing in a language accepted by that Authority has not been furnished, the Authority may invite the applicant to furnish such a listing (or a translation of language-dependent free text) and, if applicable, to pay a late furnishing fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sequence listing required by ISA is for the purposes of carrying out the international search only; national law governs disclosure in national phase. Refs: Rule 5.2, Rule 13ter.1, Annex C, paragraph 5.099.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommended software for electronic sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau recommends creating the sequence listing using WIPO Sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to paragraph 5.104 for details; WIPO Sequence produces the electronic format expected by Authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labeling electronic carriers containing sequence listings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any diskette or other electronic carrier acceptable to the ISA must have a label permanently affixed with the applicant's name, title of the invention, reference number, date data were recorded, computer operating system and name of competent Authority; if submitted after filing, labels must also include the filing date and application number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Based on Annex F - Appendix IV - 2.(f) of the Administrative Instructions; label must be typed or hand-printed in block capitals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for furnishing a sequence listing upon invitation (time limits and fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invitation to furnish a sequence listing will specify a time limit for response and may require payment of a late furnishing fee (not exceeding 25% of the international filing fee excluding extra-sheet fees). Any sequence listing furnished must be accompanied by a statement that it does not go beyond the disclosure in the application. Failure to comply may result in the search being restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amount of late fee determined by ISA but capped at 25% of filing fee (excluding extra sheets). Means of submitting documents: paragraphs 11.067–11.070.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing furnished to ISA does not form part of the international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Any sequence listing furnished separately to the ISA under Rule 13ter is used only for the purposes of the international search and does not form part of the international application; however, once the international application is published the listing will be made available for public inspection and the applicant may later amend the description to include a sequence listing complying with ST.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listing is published on PATENTSCOPE after publication; applicant may include the listing at Article 34 or national phase entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing requirements also apply during international preliminary examination and to designated Offices
rubrics_metrics.description: The same requirements for sequence listings for international search apply during international preliminary examination; an IPEA may invite the applicant to furnish a compliant listing or translation. Designated Offices may not require a listing other than one complying with Annex C, but may invite the applicant to correct non-compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refs: Rule 13ter.2, Rule 49.5(a-bis). Consult National Chapters for designated Office practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter exclusions from international search
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA is not required to perform an international search on claims relating to: (i) scientific and mathematical theories, (ii) plant or animal varieties or essentially biological processes for production of plants/animals (other than microbiological processes and their products), (iii) schemes/rules/methods of doing business, performing purely mental acts or playing games, (iv) methods for treatment of the human/animal body by surgery or therapy and diagnostic methods, (v) mere presentation of information, and (vi) computer programs to the extent the Authority is not equipped to search prior art concerning such programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some ISAs in practice do search some of these fields to varying extents—see Annex D for details. Also, ISA may decline to search where a meaningful search cannot be carried out (e.g., missing compliant sequence listing). If ISA declines to search any claims it may declare it will not establish an ISR; lack of ISR does not affect application validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to search unclear or defective international applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA considers the description, claims or drawings fail to comply with prescribed requirements to such an extent that a meaningful search cannot be carried out (e.g., unclear description or claims), it may declare it will not establish a search report, in whole or in part. Where only some claims are unsearchable, it will establish a partial search report for the searched claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial search report contains declaration under Article 17(2)(b) that certain claims were unsearchable. Multiple dependent claims not complying with Rule 6.4(a) second/third sentences may be unsearchable (see paragraph 5.113).

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity of invention requirement for entitlement to search fee coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: The international application must relate to only one invention or to a group of inventions so linked as to form a single general inventive concept (unity of invention). The search fee is intended to compensate the ISA only where the application meets this unity requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further explanation and tests for unity are in paragraphs 5.114–5.123 and Rule 13. Failure to meet unity leads to invitation for additional fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitation to pay additional fees when lack of unity found (content and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA finds lack of unity of invention, it invites the applicant to pay additional fees, specifying reasons for its finding and indicating the number of additional fees to be paid; the invitation will also invite payment of a protest fee where applicable. Additional fees are payable directly to the ISA within one month from the date of the invitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annex D indicates the amount of additional search fees per additional invention charged by each ISA. Payment within one month; failure to pay means those parts not searched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial search annexed when inviting for additional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: When inviting the applicant to pay additional fees, the ISA may annex results of a partial international search limited to the invention first mentioned in the claims (identified in the invitation); results will be included in the ISR when established together with results of searches for any further invention for which the applicant pays the additional fee within the fixed time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial search relates to the 'main invention' first mentioned in the claims; see paragraph 7.018.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISR established at least on main invention and paid-for further inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA establishes the international search report on those parts relating to the 'main invention' (first mentioned in the claims) and also on any invention or group of inventions for which the applicant has paid the additional fee within the invitation time limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures main invention is always searched even if other parts are not paid for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to pay additional fees under protest and review procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may pay additional fees 'under protest' accompanied by a reasoned statement that the application complies with unity or that required additional fees are excessive; such protest is examined by a review body constituted within the ISA and a decision taken. If protest is justified, additional fees are wholly or partly reimbursed. At applicant's request, texts of both protest and decision are notified to designated Offices with the ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refs: Rule 40.2(c),(d). The protest procedure may include reimbursement and transmission of documents to designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest fee for examination of protest (payment consequence)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the applicant pays additional fees under protest, the ISA may require payment of a protest fee for examination of the protest; details appear in Annex D. If the applicant fails to pay any required protest fee within one month from the invitation date, the protest is considered not to have been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to pay protest fee within one month leads to protest being treated as not made; check Annex D for amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of not paying additional fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant does not pay all additional fees within the prescribed time limit (or pays only some), certain parts of the international application are not searched. The lack of ISR for those parts does not by itself affect validity or processing of the international application, but some national laws of designated States may consider unsearched parts withdrawn unless a special fee is paid to the national Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only a few national Offices apply such provisions; details of special fees are in National Chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISA may establish title or abstract when missing or defective
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ISA finds the title or abstract missing or defective, in certain circumstances the ISA may eventually establish an appropriate title or abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Rules 37, 38 and 44.2 and paragraph 5.173 for details on when and how ISA may do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for establishment of the international search report (ISR)
rubrics_metrics.description: The international search report must be established within three months from the receipt of the search copy by the ISA or within nine months from the priority date, whichever time limit expires later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Article 18(1), Rule 42. These are strict procedural limits for ISR issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of the international search report
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISR must contain citation of documents considered relevant, classification of the subject matter (IPC), an indication of fields searched (identified by classification) and any electronic database searched (including, where practicable, the search terms used). Citations of particular relevance must be specially indicated; citations not relevant to all claims must be related to the specific claim(s); relevant passages must be identified (page/column/lines). An ISR must not contain any expression of opinion, reasoning, argument or explanation of any kind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full details in Rule 43. Emphasis that ISR is purely a citation/classification document, not an opinion piece.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission and publication of ISR and written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA transmits, on the same day, one copy of the ISR (or declaration that none is established) and the written opinion to the applicant and to the International Bureau. The International Bureau publishes the ISR with the published international application and sends a copy to the designated Offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Article 18(2), Rule 44.1. Ensures simultaneous communication to applicant and IB; IB publishes on PATENTSCOPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant response opportunities to ISR and written opinion
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulations do not specifically provide an opportunity to respond to the ISR, except that under Article 19 the applicant has one opportunity to amend the claims. For the written opinion, applicants may submit informal comments to the International Bureau to rebut the written opinion if international preliminary examination is not requested; there is no maximum word count for informal comments and they should be clearly identified as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal comments will be made publicly available on PATENTSCOPE; recommended to submit before 28 months from priority to ensure availability to designated Offices upon national phase entry. Comments after 30 months will be kept in IB file but not transmitted. Formal responses must be filed with an IPEA under Article 34 as part of Chapter II; if a demand for Chapter II is filed, informal comments under Chapter I will not be forwarded to designated Offices but remain public.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to obtain copies of documents cited in the ISR
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant can obtain copies of the documents cited in the ISR by requesting them from the ISA. Some ISAs transmit such copies automatically without extra charge; for others fees are charged (see Annex D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check Annex D for which ISAs supply copies automatically and the fees charged by others.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and timing of the written opinion of the ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: The ISA establishes, at the same time as the ISR or accompanying declaration, a preliminary and non‑binding written opinion on whether the claimed invention appears to be novel, to involve an inventive step and to be industrially applicable (similar in scope to the written opinion by IPEA). The written opinion is established within the same time limits as the ISR (3 months from receipt of the search copy or 9 months from priority date) and is in the language in which the ISR is established.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Rule 43bis.1(a), Article 18(1), Rule 42. The relevant prior‑art date for the written opinion is the international filing date or the priority date where priority claimed (different from the date used in establishing the ISR).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship between ISA written opinion and international preliminary report on patentability (IPRP Chapter I)
rubrics_metrics.description: If no international preliminary examination report (Chapter II) has been or will be established, the ISA written opinion will form the basis for the issuance by the International Bureau (on behalf of the ISA) of the IPRP (Chapter I), which will be communicated to all designated Offices (together with any informal comments submitted by the applicant). The IPRP (Chapter I) is made available on PATENTSCOPE after 30 months from priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a demand for IPE is filed, the ISA written opinion will generally be used by the IPEA as its own first written opinion unless the IPEA notifies otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and purpose of supplementary international search (SIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary international search permits the applicant to request, in addition to the main international search, one or more supplementary searches each to be carried out by an International Authority other than the ISA that carried out the main international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Rule 45bis. SIS expands linguistic and technical scope and reduces risk of new prior art appearing in national phase; see paragraph 8.002 for benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Which Authorities can carry out a supplementary international search
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an ISA that has stated its preparedness to carry out supplementary international searches (listed in Annex SISA), and which is not the ISA that carried out the main international search, can be requested to carry out a supplementary international search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also see Rule 45bis.1(e) and Annex SISA; applicant must choose eligible Authority different from main ISA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorities may specify limitations and conditions on supplementary searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorities offering supplementary international searches may specify any limitations and conditions on the service (per their agreement with the International Bureau). These limitations may include subject-matter limits beyond those applicable to the main international search and limits on the total number of supplementary searches carried out in a given period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Rule 45bis.9(a),(c), Annex SISA and ISA–IB agreements available online for specific limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing a supplementary search request
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for a supplementary international search must be filed prior to the expiration of 22 months from the priority date (requests received after that time will be considered not submitted). In many cases requests are filed after receipt of the main ISR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No provision for extension beyond the 22‑month time limit; see Rule 45bis.1(a), Rule 45bis.1(e)(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and recommended filing method for supplementary search request
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of Form PCT/IB/375 'Supplementary Search Request' is optional but highly recommended; the editable PDF is available on WIPO's website and it is recommended to submit via ePCT to the International Bureau.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete form according to the Notes attached. Form facilitates preparation and processing; see Section 102(f),(g) and online instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple supplementary search requests require separate forms
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant wishes more than one supplementary international search, a separate request (preferably using Form PCT/IB/375) should be submitted for each supplementary international search requested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Rule 45bis.1(a). Submit separate requests to specify different Authorities or conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to file the supplementary search request
rubrics_metrics.description: A supplementary search request must be filed with the International Bureau, not with the Authority specified for supplementary search. The IB will transmit the request to the specified Authority after verifying that all formal requirements have been complied with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Rule 45bis.1(b), Rule 45bis.4(e). Do not file directly with the Authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements for the supplementary search request and correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: The supplementary search request should be filed in either English or French. Correspondence between the applicant and the International Bureau should be in English or French (provided it is in the same language as the international application when filed in English or French). Communications via ePCT may also be in the language of publication of the international application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Rule 92.2(d), Section 104. Choose language consistent with application to avoid translation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to identify the Authority specified for supplementary search on the form
rubrics_metrics.description: The Authority specified for supplementary search should be identified by indicating the name or two‑letter code of the Authority at the top of the first sheet of Form PCT/IB/375.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Rule 45bis.1(b)(ii). Use correct code/name to avoid processing delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documents to submit with supplementary search request (translations and sequence listings)
rubrics_metrics.description: If neither the language of filing nor a furnished translation is accepted by the Authority specified for supplementary search, a translation into a language accepted by that Authority must be submitted with the request. If the application contains nucleotide/amino acid sequences, the applicant should, if required, furnish a sequence listing complying with Annex C in a language accepted by that Authority to the International Bureau together with the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Rule 13ter.1, Rule 45bis.1(c). Ensure compliance with Annex C (ST.26) and language acceptance to avoid rejection or delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the international application in Box I of the supplementary search request
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant should clearly identify the international application by its international application number, international filing date (use specified date format) and title, as provided for in Box No. I. If a new title has been established by the ISA, that title should be indicated. Where several priorities claimed, the earliest filing date should be indicated as the priority date; a file reference not exceeding 25 characters may be added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Rule 45bis.1(b)(i), Section 109, Section 110. Accurate identification avoids misrouting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of applicant in Box II of the supplementary search request
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant should be identified by name and address in Box No. II; the requirements are the same as for the request form (PCT/RO/101). If there are multiple applicants only one needs to be indicated (recommended to indicate the applicant who will represent all and receive notifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ref: Rule 45bis.1(b)(i). If agent/common representative is indicated in Box III, notices will be sent to that agent. Provide an e‑mail address if electronic notifications are desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic notification option and applicant responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: If an e‑mail address is indicated in Box II, the International Bureau (and the Authority specified for supplementary search, if it provides the service) will send notifications by e‑mail and usually not by paper mail. If an agent has provided an e‑mail address, notifications will typically be sent only to the agent. Applicants are responsible for keeping e‑mail up‑to‑date and ensuring incoming e‑mails are not blocked; changes should be requested to be recorded, preferably directly at the International Bureau under Rule 92bis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not all Authorities send notifications by e‑mail—check Annex B. Option to receive notifications exclusively by postal mail by marking checkbox.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment of agent for procedures before the Authority specified for supplementary search
rubrics_metrics.description: An appointment of an agent to represent the applicant for international phase procedures (including those before the Authority specified for supplementary search) may be made in Box IV of Form PCT/RO/101 or by separate power of attorney submitted to the receiving Office. If an agent is to be appointed specifically for procedures before the Authority specified for supplementary search, indicate this in Box No. III of the supplementary search request form and have the form signed by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refs: Rule 45bis.1(b)(i), Rule 90.1–90.5 and paragraphs 5.041–5.046, 11.001–11.014. Ensure correct signature and designation to effect representation.
